summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of molybdenum sulfide (MoS_x) on porous carbon fiber papers (CFPs) using molybdenum hexacarbonyl and dimethyldisulfide as precursors. The ALD process results in the growth of particle-like MoS_x on the CFPs due to the lack of adsorption sites, and its crystallographic structure is a mixture of amorphous and nanocrystalline phases. The ALD-MoS_x/CFP catalysts exhibit excellent catalytic stability due to the strong adhesion of MoS_x on the CFP and the mixed phase. The study investigates the electrochemical hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity and stability of the catalysts.
